angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 680,742 km at 139.74 pc = 0.07 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 7.1564 +/- 0.0104 mas (same row, RUWE 0.89): 139.74 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.9785 +/- 0.0175 solar radii from MacDougall et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-1249 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...33M/abstract): 680,742 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.0062 +/- 0.0318 solar masses from MacDougall et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-1249 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...33M/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5497 +/- 69 K from MacDougall et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1249 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...33M/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: MacDougall et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1249 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...33M/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-1249.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.460, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
